images.caption: Landguard Fort. Site of the Last Major Opposed Invasion of England and the First Land Battle of English Marines in 1667, it is now a large Victorian Fort, which has been used by Coastal Artillery, Royal Engineers (for Sea Mines), Royal Navy (for Signalling and Boom Defence) and Royal Air Force (as Seaward Defence Headquarters). Landguard overlooks the Orwell Estuary.

images.caption:
Landguard Fort, at the mouth of the River Orwell in Suffolk.


"Landguard Fort,on the Suffolk side of the estuary of the two
rivers, completely commands the entrance to the harbours of
Harwich and Ipswich. It is a strong fortification, on a small
neck of land so situated as to become an island at high-water,
nearly a mile from the shore. It was enlarged in the present
century, and is now mounted with a battery of eleven heavy guns,
on revolving frames, and twenty-five others of various calibre
on the outworks, which give to the whole a very formidable
appearance."
images.alt:
Landguard Fort, at the mouth of the River Orwell in Suffolk.
